title: Characterization of Patients with AML
summary:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is one of the diseases of the hematopoietic system with the shortest median survival time after diagnosis and, despite significant therapeutic advances, continues to be a disease associated with high mortality. In many cases, it develops from a myelodysplastic syndrome.  Over the past few decades, patient survival has improved, particularly due to the introduction of effective anti-infective measures. 
In addition, the approval and implementation of new antineoplastic agents such as gemtuzumab ozogamicin, midostaurin, and venetoclax have led to further significant advances in the treatment and prognosis of the disease.
Since AML originates in the bone marrow and, for a significant proportion of patients, an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant is the only therapy with curative potential, this form of treatment plays a central role in the overall therapeutic approach. 
The care of patients with AML therefore requires a highly complex, interdisciplinary treatment approach in which supportive care, drug therapy, molecular diagnostics, and transplant procedures must be closely coordinated. Against this backdrop, the systematic analysis of patients treated at our institution is of particular importance.
By retrospectively characterizing the patient population and by collecting and analyzing individual patient treatment outcomes—taking into account clinical, biological, and disease-specific characteristics—it is possible to assess the extent to which the results achieved at our own center are comparable to the data published in the literature. In addition, the study makes it possible to identify potential strengths and weaknesses in existing care structures and treatment processes at the facility. 
The findings can thus make an important contribution to quality assurance and the continuous improvement of patient care. In addition, they can help to better understand prognostic factors in the local patient cohort, evaluate the implementation of new therapeutic approaches in clinical practice, and identify areas of focus for future research projects as well as for the further development of personalized treatment strategies. Overall, the study is expected to yield valuable insights for the care of patients with AML at our own center and thus indirectly contribute to improving future treatment outcomes.
